title: Sales vs Previous Year

views.label: Jan-Dec 2023

hero.verdict_tag: Top line only for this period
hero.headline: Jan-Dec 2023 Revenue was 105.0M, down -4.23% against the same period last year, while Units rose +1.99%.
hero.narrative: Revenue finished at 105.0M, down -4.23% against the same period last year. Read two ways, the business took less Revenue from a larger unit base: Units rose +1.99% to 49.1M while Price fell -6.10% to 2.14. That means the result was driven by lower average revenue per item, not weaker unit demand. The category risk is broad: 63.3% of categories declined, and those declining areas carry 55.3% of Revenue.

contributions.note: HOME & LIVING carries the group (+0.67 pts) while TECHNOLOGY drags it (-1.82 pts).

cards.story: TECHNOLOGY was the sharpest drag on the year: Revenue fell -20.10% and reduced the group by -1.82 points. The drop came from transactions -8.32% and price -14.23%, while basket size rose +1.61%, so fuller baskets did not offset fewer transactions and lower value per item.

cards.state: More transactions and lower prices and mix
cards.story: FRESH FOOD cut Revenue by -6.91%, a -1.33 point drag on the group, from one of the larger parts of the business at 18.67% of Revenue. Transactions rose +3.55% and basket size rose +0.13%, but price fell -10.22%, so lower value per item outweighed the extra activity.

CONSUMER GOODS mattered most in money terms after TECHNOLOGY: Revenue fell -3.17%, down -1.5M, and reduced the group by -1.36 points. Its scale makes that important, as it still holds 43.40% of Revenue; transactions fell -5.11% and price fell -5.16%, while basket size rose +7.59%.

cards.state: More transactions, less value - revenue up
cards.story: HOME & LIVING moved against the wider result and added +0.67 points to the group with Revenue up +7.96%. That growth was led by transactions at +10.34%, while basket size fell -1.19% and price fell -0.97%, so it grew through more transactions rather than higher value per item.

LIFESTYLE slipped -4.26% and reduced the group by -0.56 points. Transactions were up +0.80% and basket size up +2.12%, but price fell -6.99%, so the decline sat in lower average revenue per item rather than weaker item movement.

Unassigned rose +2.35% and added +183K, moving ahead of the overall result by 6.1 points. It remains a meaningful part of the business at 7.60% of Revenue, but it is revenue with no department classification in the model, so it should be read separately from the named departments.

entries.headline: TECHNOLOGY Revenue changed by -2.0M.
entries.connect: TECHNOLOGY also saw Quantity change by -27.2K and Transactions change by -31.8K. CONSUMER DEVICES was the largest section drag, reducing Revenue by -1.0M. Within the department, change in units sold reduced Revenue by -678.1K, and average revenue per item and mix reduced Revenue by -1.3M.

hero.state: More transactions, less value - revenue down
hero.headline: Revenue is -1.61% - more transactions, less value - revenue down
hero.narrative: Revenue is -1.61% (-161K). Read two ways, that is +5.47% on how many bills and -6.71% on what each was worth. Underneath, transactions +548K, basket size -104K and price and mix -605K - these sum to the revenue move. Units, which strip price out, are +4.43%.
hero.reconciliation_note: Growth rates multiply rather than add. Effects are charged in reading order - transactions, then basket size, then price - so they sum exactly to the revenue change; a different order moves the shared interaction between levers.
